page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a virtual server in the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, resulting in 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key architectural consideration is the shared CPU allocation model and the reliance on network-attached storage, with only 1 GB of local storage capacity.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong performance characteristics. Single-core stress-ng CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores place it in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth for large block read and write operations is also in the top 10% tier, reaching 530.35 GB/sec and 259.87 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations also achieve top-tier status. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the system processes 5731.94 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M parameter model.

Given its shared CPU allocation, this server offers high resource density for memory-intensive and multi-threaded workloads at a lower qualitative cost profile than dedicated-core equivalents. However, the shared CPU model introduces potential performance variability under sustained peak loads. It is best suited for large-scale general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, and database operations that can tolerate shared CPU scheduling and utilize network storage.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, configured with 64 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture, it features 32 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The server relies on network storage, providing only 1 GB of local storage. In benchmark testing, it exhibits top-tier single-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth, with large-block read speeds reaching 530.35 GB/sec. It also delivers strong multi-core performance and database operations. Due to its shared CPU model and high memory capacity, this instance offers a cost-effective solution for resource-dense workloads. It is highly suited for memory-heavy applications, multi-threaded data processing, and web serving environments that do not require dedicated CPU cores.
